annotation.title_clean: امکان‌سنجی اعطای شخصیت حقوقی به ربات‌های هوشمند با تکیه بر مصوبه اتحادیه اروپا (شخص الکترونیک 2017)
annotation.title_en: Feasibility of Granting Legal Personality to Intelligent Robots, Based on the European Union Resolution (Electronic Person, 2017)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Assistant Professor, Department of Law, Payame Noor University, Iran (author name not shown in excerpt)
annotation.venue: فصلنامه مجلس و راهبرد (Majlis and Rahbord Quarterly)
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Iranian journal article examining whether intelligent robots can be granted legal personality, based on the EU Parliament's 2017 'electronic person' proposal. Using a descriptive-analytical method, it concludes personhood is currently not feasible given robots' autonomy levels, but would not be barred if robots reached full autonomy, perception and will.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous robots create a liability gap because their behaviour is unpredictable to producers and owners.
The EU proposed electronic personality for robots to protect victims.
Granting legal personality to robots is currently not feasible given their autonomy level.
If robots attain full autonomy, perception and will, nothing prevents granting personhood.
Reviews robot definitions (EN ISO 8373, Korean Intelligent Robots Act) and autonomy levels.
